claims.text: GitHub artifacts are retained for 90 days by default, are immutable since version 4, are meant to share data between jobs of one workflow, and go when the run is deleted.
claims.quote: are immutable since version 4, and are meant to "share that data with another job in the same workflow"

claims.text: The dependency cache is 10 GB per repository, and GitHub removes entries not accessed in over 7 days.
claims.quote: The dependency cache is 10 GB per repository

claims.text: Job outputs can be a maximum of 1 MB per job, and outputs containing secrets are redacted on the runner.
claims.quote: Job outputs "can be a maximum of 1 MB per job"

claims.text: All three exits live inside GitHub, readable by whoever can read the repository's runs, and none is a versioned history you can hand to someone outside it.
claims.quote: All three live inside GitHub, readable by whoever can read the repository's runs, and none is a versioned history you can hand to someone outside it.

claims.text: A CI job is compute that is gone after the task and wants a memory that is not, the same shape this site wants from its agents.
claims.quote: compute that is gone after the task, and a memory that is not. A CI job is exactly that kind of compute.

claims.text: Everything was run with sgit 0.21.0 against a local vault server, version 0.34.0 of the same package the diniscruz/sg-send-vault image runs, each job in its own empty home directory.
claims.quote: Everything below was run for this article with sgit 0.21.0 against a local vault server, version 0.34.0 of the same package

claims.text: The hyphen makes sgit clone read the key from stdin, keeping it out of the process list and the shell history.
claims.quote: The - makes sgit clone read the key from stdin, which keeps it out of the process list and the shell history.

claims.text: Once pushed to a vault, a release manager, an auditor or another company's pipeline can clone the outputs with a read key, see every run as a commit and diff two releases, without a GitHub account.
claims.quote: a release manager, an auditor or another company's pipeline can clone them with a read key, see every run as a commit, and diff two releases, without a GitHub account

claims.text: The server sees ciphertext: a search of a server's storage for the plaintext found none, in the earlier article and in this test.
claims.quote: searched a server's storage for the plaintext and found none, and so did this test.

claims.text: The release job cloned with the read key scoped to test/ and had one file on its disk, the report; the archive was never downloaded.
claims.quote: The release job cloned with the read key, scoped to test/, and on its disk there was one file, the report: the archive was never downloaded.

claims.text: When the read-key clone tried to commit, sgit answered that the vault was cloned read-only and a write needs a re-clone with the full vault key.
claims.quote: This vault was cloned read-only. To write, re-clone with the full vault key.

claims.text: A scoped clone is a speed setting, not a boundary: a job holding the full vault key can widen its clone with sgit fetch.
claims.quote: A scoped clone is a speed setting, not a boundary.

claims.text: sgit gives a pipeline four kinds of key, the vault key, the read key, an append token and a job's own key pair, and the design question is which job holds which.
claims.quote: sgit gives a pipeline four kinds of key, and the useful design question is which job holds which.

claims.text: An append token adds to one inbox of the vault's append lane and can read nothing, not even what it wrote.
claims.quote: An append token adds to one inbox of the vault's append lane and can read nothing, not even what it wrote.

claims.text: The server's access token is not a vault permission: on a private server it is the door every route needs, and an append without it was refused with 401.
claims.quote: On a private server it is the door, and every route needs it; in the test, an append without it was refused with 401.

claims.text: A pipeline where every job can do anything and the YAML promises it will not is a mandate kept by hope; one where each job's key allows only what its step is for has written the mandate as a barrier.
claims.quote: a pipeline where every job can do anything, and the YAML promises it will not, is a mandate kept by hope.

claims.text: In the test three shards each appended one entry with their token; an unknown token, a wrong enumeration key and a wrong write key were each refused with 403.
claims.quote: In the test, three shards each appended one entry with their token. An unknown token was refused with 403.

claims.text: The server caps an append entry at 5 MB and an inbox at 1,000 waiting entries, and lists at most 200 at a time.
claims.quote: The server caps an entry at 5 MB and an inbox at 1,000 waiting entries, and lists at most 200 at a time.

claims.text: A compromised shard can at worst add noise to one inbox; it cannot read the other shards' results or anything else in the vault.
claims.quote: a compromised shard can at worst add noise to one inbox; it cannot read the other shards' results, or anything else in the vault.

claims.text: sgit pki keygen makes an encryption and a signing key pair protected by a passphrase, and sgit pki export gives the public half as a small JSON file for the vault's keys folder.
claims.quote: sgit pki keygen makes an encryption and a signing key pair, the private keys protected by a passphrase

claims.text: A deploy configuration encrypted to the deploy job's key held none of the plaintext; the test job's attempt to decrypt it got Decryption failed, and the deploy job decrypted it and verified the signer.
claims.quote: The test job tried to decrypt it and got "Decryption failed".

claims.text: The deploy job verified the build job's signed manifest as valid, and after one line was appended the same check returned Signature INVALID.
claims.quote: after one line was appended to the manifest the same check returned "Signature INVALID".

claims.text: Per-job keys are not perfect key management and need not be: a pipeline wired this way fails loudly when a step reads something not meant for it, instead of quietly working until it leaks.
claims.quote: a pipeline wired this way fails loudly when a step reads something that was not meant for it, instead of quietly working until the day it leaks.

claims.text: After the build and test jobs the sidecar server's storage was 388 KB in 19 files, a search of it found no file names or contents, and archived it was 208 KB.
claims.quote: the server's storage after the build and test jobs was 388 KB in 19 files, and a search of it found none of the file names or contents.

value.unit: KB of ciphertext in the sidecar's storage after two jobs

claims.text: The storage folder can live wherever a CI system keeps bytes, the Actions cache, an artifact, a release asset or a branch, and the next run restores it with its full history.
claims.quote: So the folder can live wherever a CI system keeps bytes: the Actions cache, an artifact, a release asset, or a branch of the repository

claims.text: Reading needs no server at all, from a folder or a static host, but pushing needs the server's API, and sgit refuses to push to a folder or a static host with an error that says so.
claims.quote: Writing is different: pushing needs the server's API, and sgit refuses to push to a folder or a static host, with an error that says so.

claims.text: Archive the server's storage or a vault's bare folder, never the local folder, which holds the vault key in clear, the server token and the clone's private key; it was the only place the passphrase was found.
claims.quote: that folder holds the vault key in clear, the server token and the clone's own private key.

claims.text: The workflow is built from the commands above and not yet run on GitHub Actions; it assumes a server the jobs can reach and the keys in secrets.
claims.quote: Built from the commands above, not yet run on GitHub Actions.

claims.text: This newsroom already uses parts of this: its deploy workflow installs sgit 0.21.0 for a round trip through a vault, and the wires are drawn from vaults the site can only read.
claims.quote: Its deploy workflow installs sgit 0.21.0 for a round trip through a vault in its tests

claims.text: Everything was tested locally, not on GitHub Actions: a local server and separate home directories stood in for runners, and the workflow is a sketch.
claims.quote: Tested locally, not on GitHub Actions. Every result here is from a local server and separate home directories standing in for runners; the workflow is a sketch.

claims.text: --path is not access control: it limits what is downloaded, and the key decides what is allowed.
claims.quote: --path is not access control. It limits what is downloaded; the key decides what is allowed.

claims.text: The sidecar does not serve parallel jobs; each job's sidecar is its own, and parallel jobs need a shared server.
claims.quote: The sidecar does not serve parallel jobs. Each job's sidecar is its own; parallel jobs need a shared server.

claims.text: Per-job keys in secrets are only as separate as the secrets: if one job can read another's, the keys help with correctness, not containment.
claims.quote: Per-job keys in secrets are only as separate as the secrets. If one job can read another's secrets, the keys help with correctness, not with containment.

claims.text: Append payloads are stored as sent, so encrypt before appending if the content matters.
claims.quote: Append payloads are stored as sent. Encrypt before appending if the content matters.

claims.text: GitHub's redaction of secrets is not guaranteed in its own words, so keeping keys off the command line and out of uploaded folders still matters.
claims.quote: keeping keys off the command line and out of uploaded folders still matters.
